value.rationale: Vertex elimination is directly motivated by the longstanding small-triangulation/minimality problem for this canonical Poincaré-sphere complex. The result isolates the unique locally cheapest vertex and proves that its exceptionally small octahedral link is nevertheless maximally obstructed for a no-new-vertex star replacement because every possible filling diagonal is already occupied outside the star. This is a structural local obstruction, not an arbitrary census; it can guide simplification and relative-triangulation searches while explicitly stopping short of a global minimality theorem.
